paragraphs: One warm afternoon, a little girl named Alice sat beside her sister near a quiet riverbank.
The day felt slow. The air felt sleepy. And Alice wished something interesting would happen.
Then… A White Rabbit ran past her.
He wore a waistcoat. He carried a watch. And he hurried as he spoke.
“Oh dear. Oh dear. I shall be late.”
Alice had never seen a rabbit like that before.
And before she could think twice…
She followed him.
The Rabbit darted into a hole beneath a hedge.
And in another moment…
Down went Alice after him.
She fell and fell… past shelves and cupboards… past jars and pictures…
So slowly that she had time to wonder if she would ever reach the bottom.
At last, she landed softly in a quiet hall filled with many locked doors.
On a little glass table lay a tiny golden key.
Behind a small curtain, she found a tiny door that led to the loveliest garden she had ever seen.
But she was too big to go through.
Soon she noticed a bottle that said, “Drink me.”
After careful thought, she took a sip.
And suddenly…
She grew smaller.
Small enough to fit through the door.
But she had forgotten the key.
Then she found a little cake that said, “Eat me.”
And this time…
She grew taller than before.
And so began Alice’s curious day of growing and shrinking… and wondering who she truly was.
Soon Alice found herself in a pool of her own tears.
There she met a Mouse, a Duck, a Dodo, and many other strange creatures.
Together, they tried to dry off by running a very silly race where everyone won… and everyone received a prize.
Even Alice.
Not long after, Alice followed the White Rabbit again and found herself in a strange house.
She grew so large inside it that she nearly filled the room.
Outside, small animals tried to help her… and only made things more confusing.
At last, she shrank again and ran safely into the forest.
There, she met a quiet Caterpillar sitting on a mushroom.
He asked her a simple question.
“Who are you?”
Alice tried to answer… but she was no longer sure.
The Caterpillar told her that one side of the mushroom would make her grow… and the other would make her shrink.
With careful bites, Alice finally became her proper size again.
Soon after, she came to a house filled with pepper and noise.
Inside lived the Duchess, her sneezing baby, and a grinning Cheshire Cat.
The Cat smiled wider than any cat Alice had ever seen.
And then…
He slowly faded away… until only his smile remained.
The Cheshire Cat pointed Alice toward the Mad Hatter and the March Hare.
They were having a very strange tea party.
There was no room… but they invited her to sit anyway.
They talked in riddles. They argued about time. They poured tea from empty cups.
And though Alice tried to understand…
Wonderland made very little sense.
Feeling tired, Alice left the tea party and followed a winding path through the trees.
Soon she came upon a garden filled with bright roses… and soldiers shaped like playing cards.
They were painting white roses red.
For this was the garden of the Queen of Hearts.
The Queen loved to play croquet.
But her game was nothing like Alice had ever seen.
The balls were hedgehogs. The mallets were flamingos. And the players were always afraid.
For the Queen often cried,
“Off with their heads!”
Alice met the gentle Mock Turtle and the sad Gryphon.
They told her about their strange school days… and taught her dances that no one truly finished.
Alice listened kindly, though she understood very little.
At last, Alice was taken to a great courtroom.
There, the King and Queen of Hearts were holding a trial.
The Knave of Hearts was accused of stealing tarts.
Witnesses gave the silliest answers.
Rules changed by the minute.
And Alice began to feel braver.
As the trial grew more confusing…
Alice grew taller again.
She spoke up.
“This is only a pack of cards,” she said.
And in that moment…
The cards flew into the air.
The courtroom vanished.
The Queen disappeared.
The Rabbit faded away.
Alice opened her eyes.
She was back on the riverbank beside her sister.
The sun was setting softly.
And Wonderland had become a beautiful dream.
Alice stood and brushed the grass from her dress.
She smiled.
Though she was back in the real world…
She knew something gentle now.
That imagination can take you anywhere. That wonder makes even quiet days magical. And that dreams are a place you can always return to…
Whenever you close your eyes.
